TRANSACTION_BOUNDARY_IMPLEMENTATION.architecture: readPrincipalUnderOpenContext RESOLVES the refusal facts and RETURNS the audit obligation; it never writes. resolveRequestPrincipal discharges the obligation AFTER withDatabaseIdentityContext has returned -- i.e. after the principal-resolution transaction has committed -- by opening a SECOND unscoped context.
TRANSACTION_BOUNDARY_IMPLEMENTATION.why_the_emitter_does_not_open_its_own_co: Two independent reasons, both load-bearing. (1) Isolation: deciding WHICH transaction the write joins belongs at the request boundary, where the principal transaction's lifetime is known. (2) The entrypoint ledger: tests/database-runtime-entrypoints.test.ts requires any app/ region importing a database-reaching symbol to itself call a named CONTEXT_OPENER; had the emitter opened its own context, the selector would import a database-reaching symbol while opening none and the pinned contextualized magnitude would fall from 100 to 99, a pin outside this ceiling.
TRANSACTION_BOUNDARY_IMPLEMENTATION.emitter_precondition: lib/audit/tenancy-refusal.ts REQUIRES an open, unscoped context for the exact subject and throws TenancyRefusalAuditError otherwise -- including when the open context is organisation-scoped, which would assert the very membership the refusal denies.
TRANSACTION_BOUNDARY_IMPLEMENTATION.borrowed_transaction_case: When resolveRequestPrincipal runs inside a context it did NOT open, it cannot commit that transaction nor open a sibling (re-entry with a matching identity reuses the open transaction). Writing there is the prohibited coupling and skipping the row is prohibited best-effort, so the lane fails LOUDLY with AuthContextError rather than choosing either.
TRANSACTION_BOUNDARY_IMPLEMENTATION.fail_closed: The emission is deliberately not wrapped in try/catch. A failing audit write propagates and the request fails.
TRANSACTION_BOUNDARY_IMPLEMENTATION.measured_oracle: The test double records BEGIN/COMMIT and stamps every insert with the transaction open at the time. Measured result: txLog === ['BEGIN tx1','COMMIT tx1','BEGIN tx2','COMMIT tx2'] and the refusal insert carries txId 'tx2'. An implementation writing inside the principal transaction would stamp 'tx1' and log a single BEGIN.
TRANSACTION_BOUNDARY_IMPLEMENTATION.both_halves_proven: Isolation (the transaction identity above) AND fail-closed (a failing insert rejects loadRequestPrincipalResult, with COMMIT tx1 already logged) are asserted by two separate controls.
TRANSACTION_BOUNDARY_IMPLEMENTATION.prohibited_none_used: No service role, no SECURITY DEFINER, no RLS bypass, no SET ROLE, no nested incompatible identity context. The write runs as uellix_app under the caller's own claims.
